review_items.rationale: The fixed harness uses three fresh instances in configuration 1, pids 1/2/3, batch_size=1, actual MemoryStorage, and public try_become_leader/append/message/reconnected APIs. It constructs no Paxos messages and changes no stored protocol state. Its queue preserves emission order for each connected pair. The partition discards every message involving node 3 independently of type or outcome; raw output records loss of AcceptDecide(Item(22)) and Decide(2). The first prefix is checked on all three nodes as decided [11]; after the partition, nodes 1 and 2 are checked as decided [11,22], while node 3 remains accepted=decided=1 with [11]. Restoring transport precedes the documented reconnected(1) call. Target-produced Promise carries old boundary 1, and target-produced AcceptSync carries Delta [22], decided=sync_idx=2, matching ballot (config=1,n=1,pid=1), session=2,counter=1. The source path reconnected -> Recover -> equal-ballot Prepare -> Follower/Prepare -> matching-ballot AcceptSync is legal. No timer expiry, crash, pending batch or competing leadership is needed for this finite safety history. The implementation completes synchronously and emits Accepted at index 2 before observation. The completed flag is derived from that actual reply and the public Accept-phase report, not assumed readiness. The result records accepted=decided=compacted=2 and public read Some([Snapshotted(... Prefix([22]))]). Exclusive single-thread ownership ensures reads describe one live post-handler state; no shutdown or cached application copy intervenes. Identity case/receiver/sync_id is independent of compared contents; prefix and sync prerequisites precede the unique result and admission_alias selects sync. The expected string [11,22] comes from a prior actual leader read corroborated by node 2 and explicit proposal checks. The assertion compares all ordered contents, not only length or last value. Snapshot::create clones its input contents and merge concatenates changes, matching M-value-snapshot; M-log-contract requires decided entries not be reverted and M-snapshot-contract requires preservation through snapshots. Thus [22] versus [11,22] is a complete local counterexample to C-delta-prefix, not simply a changed metadata value. Source reconstruction explains it: sync_log assigns decided_idx=2 before create_decided_snapshot; that calls get_entries(0,2) on the receiver log of length 1. MemoryStorage returns empty for this incomplete interval, as required by Storage. The resulting empty snapshot is merged with Delta [22] and stored at compacted boundary 2. This causal explanation is source-derived; internal intermediate reads were not instrumented. The observed result itself establishes the content loss. Cargo test success only means the setup and driver completed; the controller comparison independently records violated with no parse errors. Explained alternatives and protections: Complete snapshots bypass local Delta base reconstruction and are not contradicted by this witness. The repository ValueSnapshot equality compares only latest_value; a passing latest-value test would be consistent with observed [22] and does not rebut loss of 11. Ballot, phase and sequence recovery guards are satisfied and protect against stale traffic; they do not validate Delta content alignment.

formation.explanation: Caller append buffers during Prepare or forwards to promised leader. Prepare quorum selects highest accepted round/length history; leader syncs it, preserves maximum reported decision boundary, appends pending work when not stopped, and sends AcceptSync. Accept-phase follower validates ballot, phase and sequence, persists entries and acknowledges accepted length. Leader stores one accepted index per pid and decides on configured write quorum, propagating Decide or piggybacking AcceptDecide. Reads classify entries by local decided index; application polls and consumes them.

context.explanation: BLE heartbeat rounds assess connectivity/happiness and propose ballots; manual attempt increments a ballot directly. SequencePaxos requires higher ballot before leader preparation and resets leader support. Higher Prepare flushes follower batches, persists promise, resets sequence and emits Promise. Lower-ballot accepts are rejected with NotAccepted; unseen higher accepts initiate recovery. New or recovered instances with stored promise enter Recover; equal-ballot Prepare is allowed there. Reconnect/gaps request prepare; ticks resend preparation and StopSign work. Configuration transition uses decided StopSign then caller constructs a fresh instance.

connection.explanation: Authority acquisition reads prior accepted history before creating new support: Promise metadata and optional log synchronization carry old accepted rounds and decisions into prepare quorum selection. AcceptSync reestablishes participation under a new ballot/session; old-ballot replies are excluded, old sequences ignored and gaps resynchronize. Stored decisions constrain selected history through maximum reported decided index; suffix/snapshot reconstruction must preserve its meaning. Pending leader proposals are appended after sync unless StopSign seals the log; followers forward buffered ordinary proposals after sync. Persistence and Snapshot traits supply history, while caller transport/ticks drive asynchronous propagation.

formation.explanation: Caller append buffers during Prepare or forwards to promised leader. Prepare quorum selects highest accepted round/length history; leader syncs it, preserves maximum reported decision boundary, appends pending work when not stopped, and sends AcceptSync. Accept-phase follower validates ballot, phase and sequence, persists entries and acknowledges accepted length. Leader stores one accepted index per pid and decides on configured write quorum, propagating Decide or piggybacking AcceptDecide. Reads classify entries by local decided index; application polls and consumes them.

context.explanation: BLE heartbeat rounds assess connectivity/happiness and propose ballots; manual attempt increments a ballot directly. SequencePaxos requires higher ballot before leader preparation and resets leader support. Higher Prepare flushes follower batches, persists promise, resets sequence and emits Promise. Lower-ballot accepts are rejected with NotAccepted; unseen higher accepts initiate recovery. New or recovered instances with stored promise enter Recover; equal-ballot Prepare is allowed there. Reconnect/gaps request prepare; ticks resend preparation and StopSign work. Configuration transition uses decided StopSign then caller constructs a fresh instance.

connection.explanation: Authority acquisition reads prior accepted history before creating new support: Promise metadata and optional log synchronization carry old accepted rounds and decisions into prepare quorum selection. AcceptSync reestablishes participation under a new ballot/session; old-ballot replies are excluded, old sequences ignored and gaps resynchronize. Stored decisions constrain selected history through maximum reported decided index; suffix/snapshot reconstruction must preserve its meaning. Pending leader proposals are appended after sync unless StopSign seals the log; followers forward buffered ordinary proposals after sync. Persistence and Snapshot traits supply history, while caller transport/ticks drive asynchronous propagation.

items.rationale: The fixed harness uses three fresh instances in configuration 1, pids 1/2/3, batch_size=1, actual MemoryStorage, and public try_become_leader/append/message/reconnected APIs. It constructs no Paxos messages and changes no stored protocol state. Its queue preserves emission order for each connected pair. The partition discards every message involving node 3 independently of type or outcome; raw output records loss of AcceptDecide(Item(22)) and Decide(2). The first prefix is checked on all three nodes as decided [11]; after the partition, nodes 1 and 2 are checked as decided [11,22], while node 3 remains accepted=decided=1 with [11]. Restoring transport precedes the documented reconnected(1) call. Target-produced Promise carries old boundary 1, and target-produced AcceptSync carries Delta [22], decided=sync_idx=2, matching ballot (config=1,n=1,pid=1), session=2,counter=1. The source path reconnected -> Recover -> equal-ballot Prepare -> Follower/Prepare -> matching-ballot AcceptSync is legal. No timer expiry, crash, pending batch or competing leadership is needed for this finite safety history. The implementation completes synchronously and emits Accepted at index 2 before observation. The completed flag is derived from that actual reply and the public Accept-phase report, not assumed readiness. The result records accepted=decided=compacted=2 and public read Some([Snapshotted(... Prefix([22]))]). Exclusive single-thread ownership ensures reads describe one live post-handler state; no shutdown or cached application copy intervenes. Identity case/receiver/sync_id is independent of compared contents; prefix and sync prerequisites precede the unique result and admission_alias selects sync. The expected string [11,22] comes from a prior actual leader read corroborated by node 2 and explicit proposal checks. The assertion compares all ordered contents, not only length or last value. Snapshot::create clones its input contents and merge concatenates changes, matching M-value-snapshot; M-log-contract requires decided entries not be reverted and M-snapshot-contract requires preservation through snapshots. Thus [22] versus [11,22] is a complete local counterexample to C-delta-prefix, not simply a changed metadata value. Source reconstruction explains it: sync_log assigns decided_idx=2 before create_decided_snapshot; that calls get_entries(0,2) on the receiver log of length 1. MemoryStorage returns empty for this incomplete interval, as required by Storage. The resulting empty snapshot is merged with Delta [22] and stored at compacted boundary 2. This causal explanation is source-derived; internal intermediate reads were not instrumented. The observed result itself establishes the content loss. Cargo test success only means the setup and driver completed; the controller comparison independently records violated with no parse errors. Explained alternatives and protections: Complete snapshots bypass local Delta base reconstruction and are not contradicted by this witness. The repository ValueSnapshot equality compares only latest_value; a passing latest-value test would be consistent with observed [22] and does not rebut loss of 11. Ballot, phase and sequence recovery guards are satisfied and protect against stale traffic; they do not validate Delta content alignment.
